explanation: Subtract n(n+1)/2 from the widened sum of all entries; the difference is the one extra occurrence.
correctness: The promised array contains one copy of each integer in 1..n plus one extra value x. Subtracting the exact required-range sum leaves x. Widen before multiplication to preserve arithmetic.
walkthrough: For [3,1,4,2,3], n is length-1=4. The expected sum 1+2+3+4 is 10, while the actual sum is 13. Their difference is 3, the duplicated value. Use widened arithmetic for the sum and formula before subtracting.
edgeCases: [1,1] returns 1. The promise includes every value 1..n and exactly one extra occurrence; the more general pigeonhole problem has a different contract.
timeComplexity: O(n) time: process the n+1 input entries; the range sum is constant-time arithmetic, or an additional n XOR operations in the XOR variants.
spaceComplexity: O(1) auxiliary space: scalar accumulator and range/loop variables, with no input mutation.
